bugs.what: The Lost Fleet quest text says 'Pay the wreck-right at the Reeve's Pride to bargain the fleet quiet,' but no place called 'the Reeve's Pride' was ever found despite exhausting Gullhaven (quay, high street, chandlery, harbourmaster's house, Drowned Bell, Smugglers' Stair) and the whole shore-path loop (Coast Path/Cliff Path/Tide Pools/Salt Pan Flats/Bramble Hollow/Salt-Crust Flat/Spit/Mudflats/Kelp Line/Sunken Causeway). The quest was still 'Left undone' at the game's end.
bugs.where: Saltkerns / The Lost Fleet (this hold's grief)

bugs.what: Stepping into The Smugglers' Cave (one room past the stair, then walking straight back down without going further) made all four companions declare their own hold-quests permanently 'behind us' ('Hollowbrook's behind us'... 'Cinderhall's behind us'... 'Coldpass already... Fenmarch's behind us now'... 'Coldpass, and Thornwold's behind us'), as if the point of no return had passed. I then walked the ordinary surface coast road to Fenmarch straight afterward and fully completed Brother Osk's quest there, proving the line was false. The real, correctly-worded warning ('Past this gate the holds fall behind you') only appears later, at The Pass Gate.

Weighing the Hollow Throne reported 'No oil yet: the Ironbound keep casks at Cinderhall, and the palace has its own' even though I was carrying 'a cask of Ironbound cinder-oil' the entire time (from Lay-brother Emmet in the Hearthlands), and had already used that same cask as the burn-resolution fuel for two other hold-griefs (the Hunger Barn and the Drowned Nave). The throne's burn path did not recognize the item already in my pack.
bugs.where: Marrowgate / The Hollow Throne, 'weigh the doors of the seat'

bugs.what: After the honour-guard fight, three companions were left critically wounded (Vell 1/9 hp, Brother Osk 2/8 hp, Lys 4/10 hp) with no way found to heal them; 'use dried herbs' and 'use wild herbs' only restore the player's own hp ('(hp+3)' applied to me alone), and no rest option existed in the crypts.
bugs.where: Marrowgate / The Old Crypts, honour guard fight

bugs.what: The Full Measure's room text prominently introduces 'a landlord who has heard every complaint about the tithe there is to hear,' but no 'talk to landlord' or any landlord interaction exists in the room.
Widow Kestrel explicitly asks 'Light a candle at St. Mara's shrine for me, if you pass it,' but neither the shrine's porch nor its nave offers any candle-lighting action.

'listen at the doors (free)' gives the identical line ('Nothing. Not wind, not settling timber...') both before and after the grief is fully rested via 'speak the names and the order together' — a stale line that doesn't reflect the change.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / The Hunger Barn — the Doors

bugs.what: Two unrelated NPCs in different regions are both simply named 'Sela' and share near-identical description/interaction text (both 'doesn't look up first. Looks up eventually, and takes your measure quick,' both solved the same way: read the signs / press plainly / offer in trade). A player tracking NPCs or companions by name could easily conflate them.
bugs.where: Hearthlands / The Tally-Keeper's Cottage vs. Saltkerns / Sela's Hut

bugs.what: The 'call the door's fate a draw' mediation option between Tamsin and Brother Osk is a will check, but as a Scout (no will investment) it failed (rolled 9 vs DC11) and left the quarrel permanently unresolved, confirmed by the ending epilogue ('Osk and Tamsin never settled it'). The only realistic option for a non-Envoy build is to pick a side.
bugs.where: Vale / The Empty Seat, Brother Osk vs Tamsin quarrel over the barrow doors

bugs.what: The same 'call it a draw between them' will check between Brother Osk and Vell also failed (rolled 8 vs DC11 with will+2) and stayed unresolved through the ending ('Osk and Vell never settled it') — the second of only two companion quarrels in the run, and both ended unmediated for the same reason.
bugs.where: Fenmarch / The Drowned Nave, Brother Osk vs Vell quarrel over the drowned congregation

bugs.what: Solving Vell's backstory via the Hall of Ledgers (instead of the originally-pointed Hollowbrook Keepers' Hall) closed 'The Exile's Ledger' with the line 'its asker's wish is past meeting,' and the final status lists it under 'Failed' even though the underlying truth was found and read aloud at the throne — confusing scoring for what felt like success via an alternate route.
bugs.where: Marrowgate / The Hall of Ledgers, founding ledger

bugs.what: Bailiff Vance's farewell line ('Mind the steps on your way out...') is unchanged immediately after his preferred, Crown-favoring outcome lost in The Tithe Question (granary made a common store, Crown standing -2), unlike every other Hearthlands NPC tied to that grief (Sergeant Rook, Sela, Sister Winnow, Lay-brother Emmet, Peg), who all got a new 'now it's rested' line.

confusions: No locator (bearings, hint, or NPC line) ever named where 'the Reeve's Pride' actually was, unlike every other quest destination in the Hearthlands and Saltkerns, which 'get your bearings' or an NPC always pinned down.

The Smugglers' Cave's 'this is all behind us now' companion banter and The Pass Gate's real point-of-no-return warning use near-identical language ('behind us' / 'fall behind you'), so the first one reads as final when it isn't.
It's never stated anywhere that ration items (dried/wild herbs, dried peas) heal only the player and never party members — this was only discovered by testing after a companion nearly died.

It wasn't clear whether taking the Free Companies' shortcut to Coldpass would forfeit the surface roads to Fenmarch, Thornwold, Cinderhall, and Hollowbrook; only empirically walking to Fenmarch afterward confirmed the roads were still open.

The Hollow Throne's burn requirement is phrased only as 'No oil yet,' with no explanation of what makes the Ironbound cask I was already carrying insufficient, or what distinguishes the 'right' oil from Cinderhall/the palace.

A hostile toll-camp (Sack Road Camp, Free Companies-aligned) and a hostile bandit camp (the Wreckers' Roost) share the same room names, the same free Scout 'mark the sentries' rounds' action, and the same slip-past mechanic, which makes them read as the same kind of encounter until the room flavor text clarifies one is meant to be paid/slipped and the other fought.
suggestions: Give every quest-named destination (like 'the Reeve's Pride') a bearings/locator hint the way Tithing and the Hunger Barn already have, so no named place is a dead search.
Move the 'your companions' home quests are behind you' banter from the Smugglers' Cave to the actual point of no return (The Pass Gate), or soften its wording so it isn't read as final early.
Let ration items heal the whole party (or state on the item that it's self-only) so a wounded companion isn't a permanent liability with no field remedy.
Make the Hollow Throne's burn check recognize any carried Ironbound cinder-oil cask, or rename the 'right' oil so it's clear the one already in the pack doesn't count.
Add a follow-up line for NPCs on the 'losing' side of a hold's grief resolution (e.g. Bailiff Vance) to match the reactivity already given to the winning side.
Either add a candle-lighting action at St. Mara's Shrine or drop Widow Kestrel's request, so an NPC's ask doesn't point at a verb the game doesn't have.
Add a 'talk to landlord' at the Full Measure or remove the landlord from the room description, since a named, described NPC is currently a dead end.
Rename one of the two 'Sela' NPCs (Hearthlands tally-keeper vs. Saltkerns salt-pan hermit) to avoid a same-name collision across regions.
Give companion-quarrel 'draw' options an alternate stat path (wits or grace, not just will) so builds that don't invest in will have a realistic chance to mediate instead of only ever picking a side.
Refresh ambient lines like 'listen at the doors' once a grief is rested, so room flavor confirms the change the way NPC dialogue already does.
Show quests resolved via an unexpected alternate route (like The Exile's Ledger) as a distinct 'resolved differently' state rather than folding them into 'Failed' in the final summary.
